what_happened: The the person running Athena saw that a job interrupted by a container restart loses its place in the queue. The fix for the stop-and-diagnose loop was filed as an urgent request's own retry. It now sits in plan group 8 behind older normal-priority items. Its priority cannot be raised because it already counts as dispatched. Container restarts are frequent (four in 14 hours), so this will keep happening.
cause: Priority is stored only on the queue item, and the dispatched flag locks it. Re-queuing after an interruption is not tied to the original item, so it is ranked by plan group and type, not by the priority the owner set. Nothing in the design treats an interrupted job as the same work that must resume where it was. Restarts were assumed to be rare, so no one planned for them.
prevention: An interrupted job or retry keeps its original item identity and priority and is ordered ahead of any not-yet-started item of equal or lower priority. Priority stays editable until the work finishes, not just until dispatch. The plan ordering must read the carried priority instead of re-deriving it from group or type. Tests: interrupt an urgent job, re-queue it behind old normal items, and check that it is picked first. Also check that changing the priority of a dispatched-but-interrupted item is accepted.
proposed_request: When a job is interrupted by a container restart or similar environment stop, Athena must put its retry back in the queue at the original item's priority and ahead of any item that has not started and has equal or lower priority. Priority must be changeable by the person running Athena on any item that is not currently running, including items already marked dispatched. Done when: (1) a test interrupts an urgent job while older normal items are queued, and the retry is chosen first by the drain and shown first in the plan; (2) a test shows that raising the priority of a dispatched but interrupted item succeeds and changes its plan position; (3) the plan output shows each item's priority and whether it is a resumed item; (4) the stop-and-diagnose loop fix currently sitting in plan group 8 runs ahead of the old normal items after this change lands. Do not change the ordering of items that were never interrupted.
